title: Descent and exponent independence of Cartier Kummer boundaries
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l and the families and normalizations of [def-amb-cartier-kummer-data]. Assume every positive quotient coefficient A_(E,n+1) is killed by some l^(r+1). For every ordinary etale Kummer family κ satisfying CartierEtaleKummerNormalization, there is exactly one family c with the published pro-etale Tate-line target satisfying CartierKummerRealization κ c simultaneously for every annihilating exponent. This asserts descent, exponent independence and uniqueness of the arrows only; it asserts neither coefficient-reduction compatibility, scheme-pullback compatibility nor a Chern equation.

proof.text: For each coefficient level choose an annihilating exponent. Exact comparison and the open-closed quotient give an invertible supported-source mate preserving the constant quotient. Finite Tate descent supplies the comparison with the published Tate sheaf. Transport κ by these two isomorphisms to construct c.

For two exponents use their maximum. The diagram of Kummer sequences has identity on the right G_m and the intervening power on the middle G_m and roots. Naturality identifies the relative boundaries and hence their unique supported Ext representatives. Successive scalar extension agrees with direct scalar extension. The root identity p_r=p_(s,r)p_s and the transition square in finite Tate descent show that the two transported arrows agree. This is also the exponent comparison already supplied by the ordinary pro-etale Cartier class.

The supported quotient unit is epic, so normalization fixes the source isomorphism. The Tate comparison is fixed on local pure root tensors: locally refine a root-trivializing etale object by the pro-etale tower of compatible roots. The tensor sheafification universal property fixes the comparison on that cover and then globally. Cancel the source isomorphism in the realization equation; function extensionality proves uniqueness. Empty divisors, empty schemes and the zero coefficient ring obey the same equations.

theorem cartier_kummer_descent
    (hkill : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      ((l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0)
    (κ : CartierEtaleKummerFamily l E)
    (hκ : CartierEtaleKummerNormalization l E κ) :
    ∃! c : CartierKummerFamily l E, CartierKummerRealization l E κ c
